title: Superman, a Handmaid, and a Rival Walk Into a Rainstorm!
summary:
Have you ever found an old diary in the attic and uncovered a family mystery? That's the feeling of "Three Days of Rain," a play coming back to Broadway in February 2027. And guess who's starring? David Corenswet, who flies as Superman, Yvonne Strahovski from "The Handmaid's Tale," and François Arnaud from "Heated Rivalry." Talk about a super team!

The play is like a puzzle. It follows two generations of a smart New York family. In the first act, three young people meet in a rainy loft after a parent dies. They find clues—maybe a journal, maybe a strange will—and try to figure out what really happened between their parents years ago. Then, in the second act, we jump back in time and see the parents themselves, young and full of secrets. It's funny and sad and full of surprises.

The director, Anna D. Shapiro, says it's one of the most beautiful plays she's ever worked on. She won a Tony Award, which is like an Oscar for theater. The play was written by Richard Greenberg, who passed away in 2025. The last time it was on Broadway, in 2006, it starred Paul Rudd, Bradley Cooper, and—in her very first stage role—Julia Roberts! Now a new cast will bring the rain and the mystery to life. Who knows what secrets they'll uncover?
why_it_matters: This play shows how the secrets our families keep can shape who we are, just like a diary might reveal hidden truths about your own grandparents.
